title: The faster root uplink is not forwarding
scenario: DSW1 has a direct 10 Gbps link Te1/1 to CORE, the verified root for VLAN 100. DSW1 also has Gi1/1 to DSW2, whose root path cost is 2 through its own 10 Gbps CORE link. The network uses short costs. The following are representative abbreviated teaching exhibits from the stated configuration.

exhibits.title: DSW1# show spanning-tree vlan 100 — excerpt
exhibits.text:
Root path cost: 6 through GigabitEthernet1/1
Te1/1               Altn BLK 19        128.49   P2p
Gi1/1               Root FWD 4         128.25   P2p

exhibits.title: DSW1 running configuration excerpt
exhibits.text:
interface TenGigabitEthernet1/1
 switchport mode trunk
 spanning-tree vlan 100 cost 19

question: Which cause explains the current path selection?
options: The local port number on Gi1/1 is lower, so it overrides the cost comparison.
The manual direct-link cost 19 loses to the indirect path cost 4 + 2 = 6.
The root is selected by physical interface speed rather than the configured bridge ID.
The root’s sending port ID outweighs any local cost configured on Te1/1.
explanation: CORE is explicitly established as root, and the worksheet gives DSW2's cost as 2. DSW1 adds its Gi1/1 cost 4 for a total of 6, which beats the manually assigned 19 on Te1/1. The cost comparison is decided before port IDs matter; the port's speed is not increased by changing its STP cost.
fix:
Remove the unintended per-VLAN override, then verify the displayed automatic cost and root path. With the stated short-cost method, Te1/1 should use cost 2 and become root port.
```ios DSW1
DSW1# configure terminal
DSW1(config)# interface tengigabitethernet1/1
DSW1(config-if)# no spanning-tree vlan 100 cost
DSW1(config-if)# end
DSW1# show spanning-tree vlan 100
```
Retest traffic and save only after confirming the intended root and path. Interface names in this worksheet belong to its example platform; do not paste them into an unrelated 2960 lab.

title: A replacement restores classic behavior on an interswitch link
scenario: The intended topology runs Rapid PVST+. After ASW3 is replaced, the transit link from ASW1 toward ASW3 uses legacy behavior during link changes. Host-edge configuration is unchanged. The following representative excerpts show the peer compatibility state and replacement mode.

exhibits.title: ASW1# show spanning-tree vlan 10 — excerpt
exhibits.text:
Spanning tree enabled protocol rstp
Gi0/1               Desg FWD 4         128.25   P2p Peer(STP)

question: What does the evidence identify as the mismatch?
options: ASW3 uses classic PVST+, causing classic interoperability on the link facing it.
The ASW1 transit port lacks PortFast, so it can never form a rapid handshake.
The replacement’s lower bridge priority requires classic rather than rapid transitions.
The P2p label establishes half-duplex operation and a shared physical segment.
explanation: ASW3's mode and ASW1's Peer(STP) indication identify the classic neighbor. The effect is on compatibility behavior of the connecting link; this does not prove that every host port in the network now waits 30 seconds. P2p is the point-to-point link type, not shared.
fix:
Configure the intended mode on ASW3, then verify the local mode and ASW1 peer behavior after negotiation.
```ios ASW3
ASW3# configure terminal
ASW3(config)# spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst
ASW3(config)# end
ASW3# show spanning-tree summary
ASW3# show spanning-tree vlan 10
```
If a peer remains in legacy compatibility, confirm that no legacy bridge remains and consult that platform's protocol-migration procedure. Do not enable PortFast on the transit link as a workaround or promise a fixed number of seconds for the Peer(STP) indication to disappear.
